nodes.description: The classical, lectin and alternative pathways all converge on cleavage of C3. Both classical (CH50) and alternative pathway haemolytic activity are absent, and adding purified C3 restores them in vitro.

nodes.description: Cells from C3-deficient patients show impaired monocyte-to-dendritic-cell differentiation and maturation, few switched memory B cells, reduced regulatory T-cell induction and defective Th1 induction. Antibody responses are variable: one patient failed to sustain a vaccine response, while a series of eight patients mounted normal toxoid responses with an abnormal IgG subclass pattern. The defect is therefore a skewing of adaptive immunity rather than a uniform antibody deficiency. The direction of the T-helper change is unsettled: the in vitro study (PMID:24321396) reports impaired Th1 induction from patient T cells, while the in vivo subclass data (PMID:25446578) show increased Th1-related IgG3 responses. The DECREASED modifier on the Th1 process below follows the in vitro measurement, and the IgG3 evidence item is curated as REFUTE against it.
